stem.en: Parliament passes a law that does not agree with the Constitution. Which of these can declare the law unconstitutional?

text.en: The judiciary, because courts check laws against the Constitution.
The legislature, because the House that passed a law decides if it is valid.
The executive, because it can refuse to enforce a law it dislikes.
The voters, because they can choose a new government at the next election.

explanation.en: The judiciary has the power to declare a law unconstitutional if it does not agree with the Constitution. A legislature can change its own law, but that is a different thing from testing it against the Constitution. The executive implements laws; it does not judge them. An election chooses representatives; it does not test a law.

hints.en: Which organ has the job of interpreting the Constitution and the laws?
